name: Fill-Rite FR1210G
summary: Fill-Rite's long-running 12V drum and tank pump, rated up to 15 GPM for gasoline, diesel, kerosene, E15 and B20, with a 12-foot hose and manual nozzle.
verdict:
The Fill-Rite FR1210G is the default 12V pump for drums and transfer tanks, mainly because it is approved for gasoline as well as diesel.

**Flow and fuels.** Fill-Rite rates it at up to 15 gallons per minute (57 LPM) and lists it for gasoline, diesel, kerosene, E15 and biodiesel up to B20. Many cheaper 12V pumps are diesel-only, like the [Fill-Rite FR1614](/gear/fill-rite-fr1614/). At 15 GPM, a 100-gallon transfer tank empties in under 7 minutes and a 5-gallon generator tank fills in about 20 seconds, so feather the nozzle near the top.

**What is in the kit.** The 1/4 HP motor draws about 20 amps from a 12V battery through an 18-foot cable. You get a 12-foot, 3/4-inch static-wire hose, a manual nozzle and a telescoping suction pipe that adjusts from about 20 to 34-3/4 inches to fit drums and tanks. Connect the cable with the switch off and away from the fill opening.

**Respect the duty cycle.** Fill-Rite lists a 30-minute duty cycle, so let it cool after long runs. That is rarely a limit when refueling equipment, but it matters if you empty several drums in a row. When pumping gasoline, bond and ground the drum as the manual describes.

Owners report it is durable and that parts are easy to find; the main complaint is the manual nozzle, which has no auto shutoff. For generator owners with only a few cans, a battery pump like the [TERA PUMP TRFA01](/gear/tera-pump-trfa01/) is simpler. It leads our [best fuel transfer pump](/best-fuel-transfer-pump/) roundup.
bestFor: Farms and shops refueling equipment from drums or transfer tanks

faqs.q: Can the Fill-Rite FR1210G pump gasoline?
faqs.a: Yes. Fill-Rite lists the FR1210G for gasoline, diesel, kerosene, E15 and biodiesel up to B20, which is the main reason to choose it over diesel-only 12V pumps. When pumping gasoline, ground and bond the drum or tank as the manual describes and keep the battery connection away from the fill opening.

faqs.q: How fast is the Fill-Rite FR1210G?
faqs.a: Fill-Rite rates it at up to 15 GPM (57 LPM). Real flow is lower with long hoses, a deep drum lift or an added filter. At rated flow it moves 100 gallons in under 7 minutes, well inside its 30-minute duty cycle, and it tops off a 5-gallon generator tank in seconds.

name: GPI M-150S
amazonQuery: GPI M-150S 12V 15 GPM fuel transfer pump
summary: GPI's mainstream 12V tank pump, rated at 15 GPM for gasoline up to E15, diesel up to B20 and kerosene; a common fit on pickup-bed transfer tanks.
verdict:
The GPI M-150S is the main alternative to the Fill-Rite FR1210G, with the same rated flow and a strong following on pickup-bed transfer tanks.

**Flow and fuels.** GPI rates the M-150S at up to 15 GPM (57 LPM) and lists it for gasoline up to E15, diesel up to B20 and kerosene. That matches the [Fill-Rite FR1210G](/gear/fill-rite-fr1210g/) on paper, so the choice often comes down to price, parts and which nozzle kit you want. GPI sells several versions: MU kits ship with a manual unleaded nozzle, AU kits with an automatic nozzle, and some versions come as a bare pump.

**Power and duty cycle.** The 1/5 HP motor draws about 18 amps at 12V DC, and GPI lists a duty cycle of 30 minutes on, 30 minutes off. Kit versions include an 18-foot power cord, a 3/4-inch by 12-foot hose and an adjustable suction pipe. Wire it with the supplied cord and fuse, run it from a healthy battery, and bond the tank when moving gasoline.

**Who it suits.** It fits contractors and farmers refueling machines from a truck or bulk tank. For refilling a generator from a few gas cans, it is more pump than you need; a battery hand pump like the [TERA PUMP TRFA01](/gear/tera-pump-trfa01/) costs far less. For bigger diesel equipment, the [GPI M-180S-EF](/gear/gpi-m-180s-ef/) adds 3 GPM.

Owners report steady flow and easy installation on transfer tanks; the main complaint is confusion over which kit includes what, so check the model suffix before you buy. It appears in our [best fuel transfer pump](/best-fuel-transfer-pump/) roundup.

faqs.a: On paper they are close: both are rated at 15 GPM on 12V DC and approved for gasoline, diesel and kerosene. GPI lists a 1/5 HP, 18-amp motor; Fill-Rite lists 1/4 HP and about 20 amps. Both include a 12-foot hose in kit form. Pick based on price, nozzle type and local parts support.

faqs.q: What does MU or AU mean on a GPI M-150S?
faqs.a: The suffix describes the kit. M-150S-MU versions come with a manual unleaded nozzle and M-150S-AU versions with an automatic shutoff nozzle, while some versions ship as a bare pump without a hose. Check the full model number in the listing so you know exactly what is in the box.

name: TERA PUMP TRFA01
amazonQuery: TERA PUMP TRFA01 battery fuel transfer pump
summary: A handheld battery transfer pump rated about 2.4 GPM, made for refilling generators, mowers and outboards from 2-6 gallon cans without lifting them.
verdict:
The TERA PUMP TRFA01 is the pump most homeowners actually need: it moves fuel from a gas can into a generator without lifting a heavy can to shoulder height.

**How it works.** Drop the intake tube into the can, put the discharge hose in the generator's fill neck and press the button; batteries in the handle drive a small impeller. TERA's spec sheet lists about 2.4 gallons per minute (9.2 LPM) with an 18-inch intake hose and a 35-inch discharge hose. Current versions stop automatically when the tank is full, which prevents the overflow that makes refueling a hot generator risky, and adapters fit common 2 to 6 gallon cans.

**Slow is fine here.** At 2.4 GPM, a 5-gallon can empties in about two minutes, plenty fast for a generator tank and easy to control at a narrow fill neck. TERA lists a duty cycle of 5 minutes running and 10 minutes resting, so it is not meant for drums or transfer tanks. For bulk fuel, step up to a 12V pump like the [Fill-Rite FR1210G](/gear/fill-rite-fr1210g/).

**Use it safely.** TERA lists it for gasoline, kerosene and diesel. Refuel only with the generator off and cool, keep cans on the ground outdoors, and never refuel in a garage. Newer generations claim slightly higher flow and longer hoses, so check which version you receive.

Owners report it makes generator refueling far less messy; the main complaints are battery life and the occasional auto-stop hiccup. Pair it with a [gas generator](/best-gas-generator/) plan, and see our [best fuel transfer pump](/best-fuel-transfer-pump/) roundup.

name: GPI M-180S-EF
amazonQuery: GPI M-180S-EF 12V 18 GPM fuel transfer pump
summary: The high-flow member of GPI's 12V M-series, rated at 18 GPM from a 1/4 HP motor; built for farms and fleets refueling big diesel equipment.
verdict:
The GPI M-180S-EF is the fast pump in GPI's 12V M-series, worth it on farms, fleets and job sites where big diesel tanks make every minute of pumping count.

**Flow first.** GPI rates the M-180S family at 18 GPM (about 68 LPM) from a 1/4 HP motor at 2,000 RPM, with 1-inch NPT inlet and outlet ports. That is 20% more than the 15 GPM [GPI M-150S](/gear/gpi-m-150s/) and [Fill-Rite FR1210G](/gear/fill-rite-fr1210g/). A 150-gallon tractor tank fills in a little over 8 minutes at rated flow.

**Wiring matters more.** GPI lists a current draw of about 20 amps and a duty cycle of 30 minutes on, 30 minutes off. Kit versions include an 18-foot, 12-gauge power cord and, depending on the kit, a 1-inch by 12-foot hose. Use the supplied cord and fuse, run it from a healthy battery, and never extend the cable with lighter wire.

**Check the fuel approval on your variant.** GPI markets the M-series for gasoline and diesel, but nozzles, hoses and filters differ between suffixes, and GPI's published spec sheets cover the M-180S family rather than the -EF suffix itself. Confirm the approved fuels and ethanol limits on the label before pumping gasoline, and bond and ground tanks as instructed.

Owners report fast fills on large equipment; the main complaint is the higher current draw on tired truck batteries. For a homeowner refueling a generator, this is far more pump than needed; a [battery hand pump](/gear/tera-pump-trfa01/) is a better match. See our [best fuel transfer pump](/best-fuel-transfer-pump/) roundup.

name: Fill-Rite FR112 Hand Pump
summary: A manual rotary drum pump rated at about 10 gallons per 100 turns and approved for gasoline, diesel and kerosene; the no-power backup for any farm or shop drum.
verdict:
The Fill-Rite FR112 is the pump that works when every battery is dead, which is why every farm or shop with a fuel drum should keep one.

**No motor, no wiring.** It threads into a standard 2-inch drum bung and moves fuel with each turn of the crank. Fill-Rite rates it at about 10 gallons per 100 revolutions, so filling a 5-gallon can takes around 50 turns. Nothing electrical sits near the vapor, and there is no duty cycle to watch.

**Approved for the common fuels.** Fill-Rite lists the FR112 for diesel, gasoline, kerosene, mineral spirits, heptane and Stoddard solvents, and retailers add E15 and biodiesel up to B20. The kit includes a telescoping steel suction pipe that adjusts from about 20 to 34-1/2 inches, an 8-foot hose with a static ground wire and a nozzle spout. Bond and ground the drum as the manual describes, especially with gasoline. Fill-Rite warns against using it to fuel aircraft.

**Know the trade-offs.** It is slower and more tiring than any electric pump, and with no auto-stop you have to watch the receiving tank. For daily equipment refueling, a 12V pump like the [Fill-Rite FR1210G](/gear/fill-rite-fr1210g/) saves time; keep the FR112 as the backup. For generator refueling from cans, the [TERA PUMP TRFA01](/gear/tera-pump-trfa01/) is lighter work.

Owners report it is close to indestructible; the main complaint is arm fatigue on large transfers. It is the hand-pump pick in our [best fuel transfer pump](/best-fuel-transfer-pump/) roundup.

name: Fill-Rite FR1614
amazonQuery: Fill-Rite FR1614 12V 10 GPM diesel transfer pump
summary: A portable 12V diesel pump rated at 10 GPM, with 8-foot suction and discharge hoses and battery clips; a budget-friendly way to move diesel between tanks.
verdict:
The Fill-Rite FR1614 is a portable, budget-friendly way to move diesel with 12V power, as long as you never need it for gasoline.

**Portable by design.** Unlike drum-mounted pumps, the FR1614 is a carry-handle pump with an 8-foot PVC suction hose and an 8-foot discharge hose, so you can set it between any two containers. It clips to a 12V battery with a 6-foot, 12-gauge cable and a 30-amp fuse, and it comes with a plastic manual nozzle and an inlet strainer. Fill-Rite rates it at 10 GPM (38 LPM) from a 1/5 HP motor, with a 30-minute duty cycle.

**Diesel only.** Fill-Rite designs it for diesel fuel, and listings warn against using it for gasoline or alcohol. That rules it out for most home generator owners, since most portable generators run on gasoline. For gasoline and diesel from one pump, the [Fill-Rite FR1210G](/gear/fill-rite-fr1210g/) or [GPI M-150S](/gear/gpi-m-150s/) is the right buy.

**Where it shines.** It suits a diesel tractor, a diesel generator or a skid steer, especially when you want to move the pump around rather than bolt it to one drum. At 10 GPM, it fills a 50-gallon tank in about 5 minutes, with plenty of margin inside the duty cycle.

Owners report good value for occasional diesel transfers; the main complaints are the basic plastic nozzle and the diesel-only limit. Compare the field in our [best fuel transfer pump](/best-fuel-transfer-pump/) roundup.
